story: In 2015 El Salvador was the murder capital of the world, with gangs like MS-13 controlling whole neighbourhoods. Nayib Bukele, a former advertising executive who calls himself the world's "coolest dictator," declared a state of exception in 2022 and has kept it renewed ever since, jailing more than 80,000 people, about 1 in 60 adults, many without trial. Murders collapsed, and Bukele became the most popular leader in the hemisphere. He has used that popularity to remove every limit on his power.

In 2024 he won a second term despite a constitutional ban, after judges his party appointed reinterpreted the rule. In August 2025, his party's legislators, holding 57 of 60 seats, approved indefinite presidential re-election, extended the term to six years and scrapped runoffs (AP via Fox Baltimore). They also cut his current term short by two years, moving the next general election to March 2027, so he can win a longer term sooner. "Democracy in El Salvador has died," said one of the three opposition deputies who voted no. Human rights lawyers and journalists who documented abuses in his prisons, including the anti-corruption lawyer Ruth López, have been arrested or forced into exile (News Central). His mega-prison CECOT, which houses deportees sent by the Trump administration, has made him Washington's most useful ally in the region. In 2026 the country is effectively in campaign season for a vote whose result few doubt.
briefing.power: Formally a presidential republic; in practice power is concentrated in Bukele, whose New Ideas party controls the Legislative Assembly, the Supreme Court and the attorney general's office. Constitutional guarantees remain suspended under the state of exception.
